title: Grateful Dead Live at Farrell Hall (SUNY) on 1970-05-08
lineage: Unknown Mic (onstage) > Cassettte Master > Sony TC-WE475 > Sony R500 (Pass Through) > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude Professional v8.01 > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Poor, tin‑can audience recording captures a rare Dark Star→Dancin' sequence with standout jams despite the awful sound.
ai_review.review: The tape is notorious for its muffled, distorted audio – reviewers liken it to a mic in a tin can or an overloaded bass monitor.  Nonetheless the performance shines, especially the long Dark Star that segues into Dancin’ In The Streets, plus a fiery Good Lovin' and a memorable Uncle John’s that many fans deem essential listening for this era.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers condemn the recording quality (poor‑to‑unlistenable) but praise the rarity and strength of the Dark Star/Dancin' segment and other jams; weighting show quality higher yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muffled, tin‑can like sound; heavy distortion, overloaded bass, low fidelity mic placement near stage/monitor; occasional moments of clarity in Dark Star but overall hard to listen.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fragmented recording but the highlighted Dark Star→Dancin' transition is praised as unique; other parts of the set are considered less compelling, yet overall the rare 1970 material is valued by collectors.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar work on Dark Star and Good Lovin' receives high praise, described as soaring and smoldering.
band_member_comments.Phil: A short bass solo in Good Lovin' is noted; overall Phil's playing is mentioned positively in a few reviews.
